scope: Actual V0,V1,O1,C1 source events and original 14-context packet; citation locator format excluded as requested.

cases.question: how to evaluate a stock
cases.assessment: Useful broad starting explanation; needs historical framing. Citation locator format excluded from semantic assessment.

issues.excerpt: companies like Coca-Cola and Gillette that dominate their fields
issues.issue: Unqualified present-tense use of a 1996 forecast; retain dated operating requirements, leadership uncertainty and overpayment warning.

cases.question: How would I work out what a company is worth before deciding whether its shares are a bargain?
cases.assessment: Useful cash-flow, uncertainty and per-share explanation; not accepted as written.

issues.excerpt: plus a risk premium appropriate for the business
issues.issue: Unsupported added valuation rule; 1998 packet discussion rejects higher discount rates as compensation for ignorance. That 1998 context was not selected for V1; notes cannot replace the missing original.

issues.excerpt: Buffett accepted as a reasonable framework
issues.issue: Overstates response to audience assumptions. General cash-distribution approach was accepted with doubts about variables/lower growth; 20-year/7% inputs were not validated.

cases.question: What makes reported profit different from cash an owner can actually take out of a business?
cases.assessment: Main formula and working-capital subtraction are useful and correct, but later statements contradict the full formula; not accepted as written.

issues.issue: Replaces c > full b with capex > depreciation, and extends inequality across sectors merely because c is significant. Inserting depreciation as the meaning of b changes the source.
Conflates EBITDA with all noncash addbacks. Also transfers the 1986 a+b cash-flow shorthand exception for some businesses into an EBITDA endorsement.

cases.question: How can I tell whether I really understand a business, rather than just know its products?
cases.assessment: Helpful product/enterprise distinction and finance-company example; not accepted as written because certainty tests and universal conditions overstate the sources.

issues.excerpt: genuine understanding produces a feeling of certainty
issues.issue: Reverses the warning: doubt is reason to stay out, but absence of doubt/feeling certain does not prove competence. Most reliable test is unsupported.

issues.excerpt: If you cannot describe why the business will still be strong a decade from now, you do not understand it
issues.issue: Turns a preference for highly predictable investments into a universal definition of understanding; historical company judgments also lose their date/conditions.

issues.excerpt: did not regard the whole enterprise as within his competence
issues.issue: Drops necessarily and the specific uncertainty about funding independently of Berkshire credit. Generic funding needs does not preserve that condition.

limits: Not a whole-corpus audit, controlled model comparison, user test or certification.
Correct formula in one paragraph does not cure contradictory claims elsewhere.
